# SwiftShot image stitcher

Reused source: [ImageStitcher.swift](https://github.com/pirzada-ahmadfaraz/swiftshot-mac/blob/0066e07095c51b224447067d5eb89401642e1d5f/Sources/CleanShotClone/Capture/ImageStitcher.swift).

Upstream revision: `0066e07095c51b224447067d5eb89401642e1d5f`.
Original source SHA-256: `002ca2744e3d995516dd5fdf552580492e356ca64d385f07bb3d8bce40fc27c6`.
Copyright (c) 2026 Ahmad Faraz. MIT license: [SwiftShot-LICENSE.txt](SwiftShot-LICENSE.txt).

Dial changes: the upstream enum is renamed to private `SwiftShotImageStitcher`; the unmatched `appendFullFrame` gap fallback is removed. The matching thresholds, signatures, candidate search, pixel verification, and footer detection are retained. Upstream row-copy routines remain in the source for attribution but production composition uses Dial's disk-backed row store. A new `ScrollingImageStitcher` adapter converts validated RGBA capture frames to CGImage, commits only successful appends, accounts for deferred footer rows, and enforces 8 million viewport pixels, a standard 40 million output pixel budget, 20,000 output rows, and 200 accepted frames. Automatic whole-page mode uses an unlinked private scratch file and a separate 512 million output pixel, 1 million row, and 4,000 frame budget. Stationary, rejected, and limit results do not update the reference or output.

The upstream project describes itself as a personal project. Its matching logic is reused as a candidate, with no maturity or native acceptance claim. Matching is sampled and relative; tolerating stationary/animated pixels does not ensure fixed sidebars are composed only once. Native page boundaries remain the capture coordinator's responsibility.

Adapter verification: the reused matcher proposes an offset; it cannot authorize an append by itself. Dial checks every RGB pixel when classifying contiguous stationary side columns, never excludes internal columns, and requires a remaining span at least 32 pixels and 20 percent of the viewport width. A packed moving-span retry can propose offsets hidden by wider stationary regions. The existing ScrollStitcher must independently accept the same offset with its dense full-pixel, texture, and ambiguity checks on a body excluding at most 15 percent at the top and a densely unchanged, matched footer capped at 25 percent. When both upstream proposals miss a valid offset, this same strict dense matcher may supply the offset as a fallback; Dial's row store performs composition only after that independent dense match. This permits verified small final scrolls without appending an unmatched frame or relaxing matcher thresholds.

Automatic page selections export the union of moving columns observed over every viewport row, including pictures outside the alignment body, removing stationary edge furniture rather than repeating it. Explicit dragged crops retain their chosen width. Visual endpoint and rollback checks compare every RGB pixel inside the previously texture- and movement-verified content body; they do not compare unrelated window furniture. Any RGB change prevents a stationary result; sparse unalignable content is rejected rather than treated as a completed endpoint. No overlap tolerance is relaxed.
